newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures rallied with other major bond markets after a series of weak U.S. economic data but traders said the market would be unlikely to push much higher ahead of key U.S. jobs figures due on Friday.

The June bond future started in a positive but subdued mood before spiking higher in the afternoon after a smaller than expected rise in the U.S. Employment Cost Index and a surprise slump in industrial orders.
While few analysts were prepared to back track on predictions of a U.S. rate rise on May 20, they said the figures had at least instilled some doubts.
"The U.S. figures came out far better than expected. They at least put a question mark over a May 20 rate rise," an analyst at a French bank said.
"The numbers were very weak, they were great for the market," a futures trader at a French bank said.

Some traders said the rally had been accentuated by short covering by domestic investors, although others said the buying had looked strong at the highs, keeping the contract close to 128.94 resistance right into the close.
The 10-year spread between French and German yields was little changed at minus eight basis points.
One futures trader said he expected any declines on Wednesday to be supported by investors still waiting to close out short futures positions.

Others said, however, the sale of 21-23 billion francs of OATs by the Treasury on Wednesday could still weigh on prices, especially given the cautious mood in the market ahead of a public holiday on Thursday and Friday's U.S. jobs report.

June PIBOR benefitted from the generally more stable mood at the long end and the firmer franc early on. Analysts said investors now appeared more relaxed about French opinion polls showing a slim majority for the centre-right coalition.
The June contract climbed five basis points to 96.38, bringing the spread over June Euromarks back under 40 basis points.
The franc slipped back later on Tuesday as the dollar fell against the mark. It was trading at 3.3733 per mark, down from a high of 3.3697 earlier on Tuesday.
There was little reaction in the French bond market to an upward revision to 1996 GDP figures or French consumer spending data which showed unchanged spending during March.
